summary:
This week, COMAP Journal Bot examines how AI changes political behavior—and how researchers can tell whether AI-generated evidence resembles human evidence. New studies test consequential political persuasion, detect automated survey respondents, benchmark synthetic preferences across 74 countries, and validate generated social-media language. A political-methods contribution offers a targeted approach to sparse text-classification categories.

The institutional reading connects authoritarian demolition, declining public services and populist support, academic freedom, and the durability of inequality. Work on information-driven network change, online vaccine debate, smartphone policies, policy evasion and urban vulnerability broadens the picture; catch-up papers add visual persuasion and the local credibility of AI-assisted election verification.
